chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Hasan al-Siqill, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) being asked about a man who bought a slave-girl and then had intercourse with her before her womb was cleared (of pregnancy). He said: 'What a bad thing he did; he should seek Allah's forgiveness and not repeat it.' I said: 'And if he sold her to another, and she had not cleared her womb, then the second man sold her to another man, and he had intercourse with her and she had not cleared her womb, and then her pregnancy became evident with the third man?' He (Abu 'Abdillah, peace be upon him) said: 'The child belongs to the one whose bed it is (the last husband), and for the adulterer is the stone.'

key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The stone (symbolizing the share or consequence for the adulterer)
key_terms.الْعَاهِرِ: The adulterer / one who has intercourse
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child belongs to the bed (husman)

ai.seo_question: How is lineage determined for a slave-girl sold multiple times while pregnant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahani, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the application of 'al-waladu lil-firash' when a slave-girl is sold multiple times before her 'istibra'' (womb-clearing) period is fully established. The Imam distinguishes between the final owner, to whom the child belongs, and the previous possessor, who receives the 'hajar' (a symbolic fine or share), emphasizing that lineage follows the last valid marital bed while penalizing prior intercourse that occurred without full legal certainty of pregnancy. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential nuance in tracking lineage and financial liability in complex sales of concubines.
